parsed.attack: The exposure is customer lifetime and channel concentration, not price. The record's value ends when the custody matter does, and kill line 3 - fewer than 10 of the first 100 payers arriving by practitioner referral - is not a metric, it is the entire acquisition plan; if the family-law referral loop does not form there is no paid substitute at any CPI, because you cannot target 'currently in a high-conflict custody case' on a bid network and family-law intent keywords run $15-50 CPC, which at a 10% click-to-install and 20% install-to-pay is $750-2,500 per paying user against a blended $5.84. There is also a wage-floor trap waiting: kill line 4 accepts nothing above 5% mis-parsed times or medication names, and if the answer to a court-facing record is human verification, one reviewed household-month at a $25 loaded rate is $12.50 against $17 of net revenue.
parsed.strongest_defence: This is the rare consumer audience that prices above the median band: TalkingParents and OurFamilyWizard already charge $10-25/month per parent, so $19.99 nets $17 after the 15% rate, the cited $20-80 cost-per-paying-user repays in 1-5 months, and a contested custody matter runs 12-36 months, so LTV is $200-600 per payer with no human ever in the loop - the parent dictates and the device transcribes.
parsed.verdict_reason: Willingness to pay sits above the $8-24 median band, marginal cost is zero, and even the top of the $20-80 acquisition band repays in five months against a multi-year litigation lifetime, so the arithmetic genuinely holds.
